decades[0].note: Prices more than doubled during the Second World War. The IGP, the index that measures the pre-IPCA era, was born at the end of the decade (backcast to 1944).
decades[1].note: Decade average (IGP-DI). Inflation was already a permanent companion to Brazilians.
decades[2].note: Acceleration to a peak of ~92% in 1964 (IGP), the height of the crisis that preceded the coup. The PAEG plan brought the pace down, at the cost of squeezing wages.
decades[3].note: The 'economic miracle' lived alongside double-digit inflation; after the 1973 oil shock, the average jumped to 51% a year.
decades[4].note: Chronic hyperinflation: an annual peak of 2,477% (1993) and ~5,000% accumulated in the 12 months to June 1994.
minimumWage.creationNote: Created by Getúlio Vargas (Decree-Law 2,162, 1 May 1940), with 14 regional levels — the highest, 240 mil-réis, in Rio de Janeiro.
minimumWage.peakNote: The minimum wage's greatest purchasing power came in the late 1950s, under president Juscelino Kubitschek (sources differ between 1957 and 1959): roughly R$ 3,000 in today's money — nearly double today's minimum. The basic food basket took less than 30% of the wage.
minimumWage.peakSource: DIEESE (via Agência Brasil) / Ipea — historical evolution of the minimum wage
minimumWage.caveat: Restated figures vary with the base date of the calculation; the divergences are documented in the methodology.
